dmv.name: Alabama Law Enforcement Agency (ALEA) Driver License Division

license.full_age: 17 after 6 months on the restricted license, or 18
license.supervised_hours: 50 hours (a driver ed course completion form can be used instead)
license.notes: Must hold the permit 6 months if under 18.

state_id.min_age: None stated on the official page

work_permit.required: no permit for the teen; employers need a Child Labor Certificate to hire anyone under 18
work_permit.issuer: Alabama Department of Workforce (issued to employers)
work_permit.notes: The old school Eligibility to Work form ended June 1, 2024; the employer gets the certificate.

youth_labor.notes: Teens 16 to 17 in school cannot work late (10 p.m. to 5 a.m.) on a night before a school day.

min_wage.notes: No state minimum wage; federal $7.25 applies.

voting.preregister_age: none; you can register if you will be 18 by Election Day

dmv.name: Alaska Division of Motor Vehicles

license.full_age: After 6 months on the provisional license with no traffic convictions, or at 18
license.supervised_hours: 40 hours, 10 in darkness or bad weather
license.notes: Must hold the permit 6 months; a parent must sign.

state_id.min_age: None; children can get one

work_permit.required: yes, ages 14 to 16 (and 17 at places that serve alcohol)
work_permit.issuer: Alaska Department of Labor and Workforce Development, Wage and Hour
work_permit.notes: The permit must be on file with the state labor department before you start.

youth_labor.notes: Anyone under 18 can work no more than 6 days a week and gets a 30 minute break after 5 hours.

min_wage.notes: Set to rise to $15.00 on July 1, 2027 under Ballot Measure 1.

dmv.name: Arizona Department of Transportation, Motor Vehicle Division (ADOT MVD)

license.full_age: Limits end after 6 months on the license (or at 18)
license.supervised_hours: 30 hours, 10 at night (or 20 hours, 6 at night, with driver ed)
license.notes: Must hold the permit 6 months.

state_id.min_age: None; any age

work_permit.notes: Arizona does not issue work permits for regular jobs.

min_wage.notes: Flagstaff has a higher city minimum.

voting.preregister_age: none; you can register if you will be 18 by the next general election

dmv.name: Arkansas Department of Finance and Administration, Office of Driver Services

license.full_age: 18, with a clean record for the past year
license.notes: Need 6 months with no serious violations or at-fault crashes to move to intermediate.

state_id.issuer: Arkansas DFA Office of Driver Services

work_permit.notes: Act 195 of 2023 ended work permits, except for entertainment jobs.

min_wage.notes: Covers employers with 4 or more workers; smaller employers may only owe the federal $7.25.

voting.preregister_age: none; you can register if you will be 18 by the next election

dmv.name: California Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV)

license.full_age: Night and passenger limits end after 12 months on the license
license.notes: Must hold the permit 6 months and finish driver ed first.

state_id.min_age: None; any age

work_permit.issuer: Your school (school district in summer)
work_permit.notes: Most teens under 18 need a work permit from their school.

youth_labor.notes: Teens 16 to 17 can work only 4 hours on a school day.

min_wage.notes: Many cities are higher, and fast food and health care have their own higher rates.

dmv.name: Colorado Division of Motor Vehicles (DMV)

license.permit_min_age: 15 with a driver ed course (15 and 6 months with a 4-hour course; 16 otherwise)
license.full_age: Night and passenger limits end after 1 year on the license
license.notes: Must hold the permit 12 months; starting Jan 1, 2027, teens 15 to 17 must take a 30-hour course before the permit.

state_id.min_age: None stated; a guardian must come with anyone under 21

work_permit.required: only for under 16 working during school hours
work_permit.issuer: School
work_permit.notes: Most teens do not need a permit outside school hours.

min_wage.notes: Denver and some other cities are higher; it rises to $15.71 in 2027.

dmv.name: Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV)

license.provisional_min_age: 16 and 4 months (with driver training) or 16 and 6 months (home training)
license.full_age: Passenger limits end after 12 months; night limit ends at 18
license.notes: Hold the permit 120 days with driver school or 180 days with home training.

state_id.min_age: None stated on the official page

work_permit.issuer: Your local school district
work_permit.notes: You need a promise of employment letter from the job to get working papers.

min_wage.notes: Changes each Jan 1 based on a set formula.

voting.preregister_age: 17 if you will be 18 by Election Day

dmv.name: Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles (DMV)

license.full_age: 17, after holding the permit 12 months
license.notes: Must finish driver ed at a Delaware high school or approved school first.

state_id.min_age: None stated; a parent or guardian must come with anyone under 18

work_permit.issuer: An issuing officer at your school or the Delaware Department of Labor
work_permit.notes: You, your employer and (if 14 or 15) a parent fill it out, then an issuing officer signs it.

youth_labor.notes: Teens 16 to 17 cannot do more than 12 hours of school and work combined in one day.

min_wage.notes: No change for 2026.

voting.preregister_age: 16 when you get a license at the DMV; otherwise you must be 18 by the next general election

dmv.name: DC Department of Motor Vehicles (DC DMV)

license.full_age: 18 (a full license with conditions is possible at 17)
license.supervised_hours: 40 hours on the permit, plus 10 night hours on the provisional license
license.notes: Learner permit holders can drive only 6 a.m. to 9 p.m.

state_id.min_age: None stated on the official page

min_wage.notes: Changes every July 1.

dmv.name: Florida Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles (FLHSMV)

license.full_age: 18 (night limits end)
license.notes: Must hold the learner's license 12 months or until 18.

work_permit.notes: Employers may ask for proof of age.

youth_labor.notes: A 2024 law (HB 49) removed some hour limits for 16 and 17 year olds.

min_wage.notes: Florida's raise date is Sept 30, not Jan 1. Starting in 2027 the rate follows inflation.

dmv.name: Georgia Department of Driver Services (DDS)

license.full_age: 18 (Class C, with no major traffic convictions in the last 12 months)
license.notes: Must hold permit 12 months and 1 day, and finish a driver ed course (Joshua's Law).

state_id.min_age: No set age. Anyone who can sign their name can apply. Under 18 needs a parent or guardian.

work_permit.issuer: School issuing officer or county school superintendent's office
work_permit.notes: You fill out a data sheet, your employer fills out a part, then the school issues the certificate.

youth_labor.notes: 16 and 17 year olds have no state hour limits. Under 16 cannot work during school hours.

min_wage.notes: Georgia's own law says $5.15, but most employers are covered by federal law and must pay $7.25.

dmv.name: County DMV / driver licensing offices (Honolulu, Maui, Hawaii, Kauai counties), under Hawaii DOT rules

license.full_age: 17, after holding the provisional license 6 months with no pending violations
license.notes: Must hold permit 180 days and finish a state-certified driver ed course (classroom and behind the wheel).

state_id.issuer: County DMV offices (program run by Hawaii DOT)

work_permit.issuer: Hawaii Dept. of Labor and Industrial Relations (16-17 apply online; 14-15 need employer and parent to file form CL-1)
work_permit.notes: Ages 16-17 get a Certificate of Age online. Ages 14-15 need a Certificate of Employment before starting.

youth_labor.notes: Every working minor under 18 needs a certificate, which is stricter than federal law. 16-17 year olds have no hour limits except during school.

min_wage.notes: Goes up to $18.00 on Jan 1, 2028.

dmv.name: Idaho Transportation Department, Division of Motor Vehicles (ITD DMV)

license.full_age: Night limit ends at 16. Passenger limit ends 6 months after you get your license.
license.notes: Must hold permit at least 6 months and finish driver ed if under 17.

state_id.min_age: No minimum age. Available to residents of all ages.

work_permit.notes: Idaho does not issue work permits for minors.

youth_labor.notes: Idaho mostly follows federal rules for workers under 16.

min_wage.notes: Same as federal. Employers can pay $4.25 to workers under 20 for their first 90 days.

dmv.name: Illinois Secretary of State, Driver Services

license.notes: Must hold permit at least 9 months.

work_permit.issuer: Your local school or school district office
work_permit.notes: Get it before you start work. The state labor department does not issue them.

youth_labor.notes: Under 16: school plus work cannot top 8 hours a day, max 3 work hours on a school day.

min_wage.notes: Workers under 18 who work less than 650 hours a year can be paid $13.00. Some local areas may set higher rates; check your city.

dmv.name: Indiana Bureau of Motor Vehicles (BMV)

license.provisional_min_age: 16 with driver ed, 16 and 270 days without
license.full_age: Night limits end at 18. Passenger limit ends after 180 days. The probationary license lasts until 21.
license.notes: Must hold permit 180 days.

state_id.min_age: No minimum age (for residents with no driver's license).

work_permit.notes: Indiana ended work permits. Employers with 5 or more teen workers must register them online.

youth_labor.notes: 16 and 17 year olds can work the same hours as adults. 14-15 year olds still have hour limits.

min_wage.notes: Same as federal.

voting.preregister_age: 17 if 18 by next general or municipal election

dmv.name: Iowa Department of Transportation, Motor Vehicle Division (Iowa DOT)

license.full_age: 17, after holding the intermediate license 12 months
license.supervised_hours: 20 hours, 2 at night (permit stage); 10 more hours, 2 at night (intermediate stage)
license.notes: Must hold permit 12 months and finish driver ed.

work_permit.notes: Iowa repealed its work permit law in 2023.

youth_labor.notes: Iowa lets 14-15 year olds work later and longer than federal rules, but employers covered by federal law must follow the stricter rule.

min_wage.notes: Same as federal.

dmv.name: Kansas Department of Revenue, Division of Vehicles (KDOR)

license.provisional_min_age: 15 (restricted to school, work and church) or 16 (less restricted)
license.full_age: 17, or after 6 months of less restricted driving at 16, whichever comes first
license.notes: Must hold permit 1 year and finish driver ed for the 15-year-old license.

state_id.issuer: Kansas Department of Revenue, Division of Vehicles
state_id.min_age: No minimum age. You can get an ID at any age.

youth_labor.notes: Under 16: no work before 7 a.m. or after 10 p.m. on school nights, max 8 hours a day and 40 a week. Federal rules are stricter for 14-15 and still apply.

min_wage.notes: Same as federal.

dmv.name: Kentucky Transportation Cabinet, Driver Licensing (Drive.ky.gov)

license.full_age: 17, after holding the intermediate license 180 days
license.notes: Must hold permit 180 days and take a driver ed course.

work_permit.notes: Kentucky does not issue work permits, but employers must keep proof of age for workers under 18.

youth_labor.notes: 16-17 year olds in school weeks: max 6 hours on a school day and 30 hours a week, unless they have parent consent and good grades.

min_wage.notes: Same as federal.

dmv.name: Louisiana Office of Motor Vehicles (OMV)

license.full_age: 17 for night limits; full license after 12 clean months on the intermediate license
license.notes: Must hold permit 180 days.

min_wage.notes: Louisiana has no state minimum wage law, so the federal $7.25 applies.

voting.preregister_age: 16 at the Office of Motor Vehicles, 17 otherwise

dmv.name: Maine Bureau of Motor Vehicles (BMV), Secretary of State

license.full_age: After 270 days on the intermediate license; a 2-year provisional period still applies for under 21
license.notes: Must hold permit 6 months and finish driver ed.

work_permit.issuer: School superintendent's office, approved by the Maine Dept. of Labor
work_permit.notes: You need a new permit for each job, and you cannot start until the Labor Dept. approves it.

youth_labor.notes: 16-17 year olds in school have limits too: 6 hours on a school day, 24 hours in a school week, done by 10:15 p.m. on school nights.

min_wage.notes: Portland and Rockland have their own local minimum wage.

dmv.name: Maryland Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA)

license.full_age: After 18 months on a provisional license with a clean record (so 18 at the earliest)
license.notes: Under 18 must hold the permit 9 months and finish driver's ed.

state_id.min_age: No minimum age listed. Under 15 needs a parent or guardian with them.

work_permit.issuer: Maryland Department of Labor (apply online)
work_permit.notes: Apply online after you get a job offer. You, a parent, and the employer all sign it.

youth_labor.notes: Ages 16 and 17 cannot do more than 12 hours of school plus work in one day, which federal law does not limit.

min_wage.notes: Workers under 18 can be paid 85% of the state rate. Some counties are higher.

dmv.name: Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV)

license.supervised_hours: 40 hours (30 if you finish a driver skills program)
license.notes: Must hold the permit 6 months and finish driver's ed; a parent must take a 2 hour class.

work_permit.issuer: Your local school superintendent's office (where the job is)
work_permit.notes: Get a new permit for every new job, even with the same employer.

youth_labor.notes: Ages 16 and 17 are limited to 9 hours a day and 48 hours a week, with no work from 10 p.m. to 6 a.m. in most jobs.

min_wage.notes: Tipped service workers can be paid $6.75 an hour plus tips.

dmv.name: Michigan Department of State (Secretary of State)

license.full_age: 17, after 6 months on Level 2 and 12 months with no tickets or at-fault crashes (Level 3)
license.notes: Must hold Level 1 for 6 months and finish both segments of driver's ed.

state_id.min_age: None

work_permit.issuer: Michigan LEO, online through the Youth Employment Permit Portal (YEPP)
work_permit.notes: Since Oct. 2, 2026, schools no longer issue work permits. Apply online.

youth_labor.notes: Every worker under 18 needs a permit, which federal law does not require.

min_wage.notes: Goes up to $15.00 on Jan 1, 2027.

car_insurance.minimum: 50/100/10 (the lowest you can pick; default is 250/500), plus PIP and $1 million PPI

dmv.name: Minnesota Driver and Vehicle Services (DVS), Department of Public Safety

license.full_age: 18, or after 12 months on a provisional license with a clean record
license.supervised_hours: 50 hours, 15 at night (40 if a parent takes a 90 minute class)
license.notes: Must hold the permit 6 months before the road test.

state_id.min_age: None

work_permit.required: no general permit; ages 14-15 need a school certificate only to work during school hours
work_permit.issuer: School district superintendent (only for school-hours work)
work_permit.notes: Most teens do not need a work permit in Minnesota.

youth_labor.notes: Ages 16 and 17 cannot work after 11 p.m. before a school day or before 5 a.m. on a school day (11:30 p.m. and 4:30 a.m. with a parent's written OK).

min_wage.notes: Workers under 20 can be paid $9.31 for their first 90 days. Minneapolis and St. Paul are higher.

dmv.name: Mississippi Department of Public Safety, Driver Service Bureau

license.notes: Must hold the permit 12 months or until age 17, whichever comes first.

min_wage.notes: No state minimum wage law; the federal $7.25 applies.

voting.preregister_age: 17 if 18 by the next general election

dmv.name: Missouri Department of Revenue, Motor Vehicle and Driver Licensing

license.notes: Must hold the permit at least 182 days.

work_permit.issuer: Your school (authorized school official)
work_permit.notes: Use the school-year form or the summer form, depending on when you work.

youth_labor.notes: State child labor law covers only workers under 16.

min_wage.notes: Some small retail or service businesses (under $500,000 in sales) are exempt.

dmv.name: Montana Motor Vehicle Division (MVD), Department of Justice

license.permit_min_age: 14 years 6 months in approved traffic ed, otherwise 16
license.provisional_min_age: 15 (after 6 months on a learner license started at 14 1/2)
license.full_age: 18, or the end date printed on the license (about 1 year), whichever comes first
license.notes: Under 18 must hold the learner license 6 months; online traffic ed does not count.

youth_labor.notes: Rules closely match federal law. Ages 14 and 15: max 3 hours on a school day and 18 in a school week.

min_wage.notes: Goes to $11.20 on Jan 1, 2027. Small businesses not covered by federal law ($110,000 or less in sales) may pay $4.00.

dmv.name: Nebraska Department of Motor Vehicles

license.full_age: After 12 months on a POP with fewer than 3 points, or at 18 when the POP expires
license.supervised_hours: 50 hours, 10 at night (or finish a DMV-approved driver safety course)
license.notes: Must hold a permit at least 6 months before the POP.

state_id.min_age: None listed. Any Nebraska resident may apply.

work_permit.issuer: School superintendent's office
work_permit.notes: The employer keeps the certificate on file while you work there.

youth_labor.notes: Ages 14 and 15 cannot work before 6 a.m. or after 10 p.m. without a special state permit.

min_wage.notes: Applies to employers with 4 or more workers.

voting.preregister_age: 17 if 18 by the general election date (first Tuesday after the first Monday in November)

dmv.name: Nevada Department of Motor Vehicles

license.full_age: 18 (night curfew lasts until 18; passenger limit lasts 6 months)
license.notes: Must hold the permit 6 months and finish driver's ed in most cases.

min_wage.notes: This rate has been in place since July 1, 2024.

dmv.name: New Hampshire Division of Motor Vehicles

license.permit_min_age: No learner's permit. You can practice at 15 1/2 with a licensed adult age 25 or older.
license.full_age: 18 (youth limits no longer apply after 18)
license.notes: Under 18 needs a parent's OK and a driver's ed certificate.

work_permit.required: yes, under 16 (youth certificate); ages 16-17 need a parent's written permission on file
work_permit.notes: Some jobs for family, casual work and farm work are exempt.

youth_labor.notes: Ages 16 and 17 in school are limited to 35 hours in a school week, which federal law does not limit.

min_wage.notes: State law uses the federal minimum wage.

dmv.name: New Jersey Motor Vehicle Commission (NJMVC)

license.full_age: 18, after 1 year of unsupervised driving on a probationary license
license.notes: Must hold permit 6 months and take 6 hours with a licensed driving instructor.

work_permit.issuer: NJ Department of Labor (online)
work_permit.notes: Get a job offer first, then apply online with your employer's code.

youth_labor.notes: All workers under 18 need working papers, and ages 14-15 are capped at 8 hours a day and 40 a week.

min_wage.notes: Seasonal workers and employers with fewer than 6 workers can pay $15.23.

dmv.name: New Mexico Motor Vehicle Division (MVD)

license.full_age: After 12 months on a provisional license with a clean record
license.notes: Must hold permit at least 6 months.

work_permit.issuer: Your school or the NM Department of Workforce Solutions
work_permit.notes: Under 16 can work up to 18 hours in a school week and 40 in a non-school week.

min_wage.notes: Statewide rate, unchanged since Jan 1, 2023.

dmv.name: New York State Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV)

license.full_age: 17 with driver ed, otherwise 18
license.notes: Must hold permit 6 months; junior drivers cannot drive in New York City.

state_id.min_age: none (any age)

work_permit.issuer: Your school
work_permit.notes: Apply at your school guidance office; moving to an online state portal in 2027.

youth_labor.notes: Ages 16-17 are capped at 28 hours a week while school is in session, which federal law does not limit.

min_wage.amount: $17.00 in NYC, Long Island and Westchester; $16.00 rest of state (2026)
min_wage.notes: Rates stay the same on Jan 1, 2027.

dmv.name: North Carolina Division of Motor Vehicles (NCDMV)

license.full_age: Full provisional after 6 months on Level 2; regular license at 18
license.notes: Must hold permit 9 months and finish driver ed.

state_id.min_age: none stated (fees listed for age 16 and under)

work_permit.issuer: NC Department of Labor (online, started by employer)
work_permit.notes: You, your parent and your employer all sign online before your first day.

youth_labor.notes: Students in grade 12 or below cannot work 11 p.m. to 5 a.m. before a school day unless parent and principal agree.

min_wage.notes: No higher state rate; same as federal.

dmv.name: North Dakota Department of Transportation (NDDOT) Driver License Division

license.notes: Ages 14-15 hold the permit 12 months or until 16 (at least 6 months) and need driver ed.

work_permit.issuer: ND Department of Labor and Human Rights (mailed form)
work_permit.notes: Teen, parent and employer sign an Employment and Age Certificate for each job.

youth_labor.notes: State rules only cover ages 14-15; federal rules still apply to 16-17.

min_wage.notes: No higher state rate; same as federal.

dmv.name: Ohio Bureau of Motor Vehicles (BMV)

license.full_age: 18 (night limits end after 24 months licensed)
license.notes: Must hold permit 6 months and finish driver ed (24 class hours plus 8 driving hours).

state_id.min_age: none

work_permit.required: yes, school-age minors (16-17 exempt for summer jobs)
work_permit.issuer: Your school district superintendent (or your school)
work_permit.notes: Called an age and schooling certificate; you must be at least 14.

youth_labor.notes: Ages 16-17 in school cannot work before 7 a.m. or after 11 p.m. on a school night.

min_wage.notes: Applies to employers with $405,000 or more in yearly sales; smaller employers pay $7.25.

dmv.name: Service Oklahoma

license.full_age: 16 and 6 months at earliest: 6 months on intermediate with driver ed, 12 months without
license.notes: Must hold permit at least 180 days.

state_id.min_age: none stated; under 18 needs a parent or guardian

work_permit.issuer: Your school (principal or school officer)
work_permit.notes: Get it approved at school before you start work; homeschool parents approve it.

min_wage.notes: Same as federal for most employers; very small employers may pay less under state law.

dmv.name: Oregon DMV (Oregon Department of Transportation)

license.full_age: 18 or after 1 year on provisional license, whichever comes first
license.supervised_hours: 100 hours, or 50 with approved driver ed
license.notes: Must hold permit 6 months.

work_permit.required: no for teens 14 and up (employer needs a certificate)
work_permit.issuer: Bureau of Labor and Industries (BOLI), to employers
work_permit.notes: Any employer hiring under 18 must hold a yearly BOLI certificate; under 14 needs a permit.

youth_labor.notes: Ages 16-17 can work up to 44 hours a week, a cap federal law does not have.

min_wage.amount: $15.55 standard; $16.80 Portland metro; $14.55 non-urban counties (since July 1, 2026)
min_wage.notes: Changes every July 1; your rate depends on where you work.

dmv.name: PennDOT Driver and Vehicle Services

license.full_age: 18 automatically, or 17 with driver ed and 12 months with no crashes or tickets
license.supervised_hours: 65 hours, 10 at night, 5 in bad weather
license.notes: Must hold permit 6 months.

work_permit.issuer: Your school district's issuing officer
work_permit.notes: You can apply in person or virtually.

youth_labor.notes: Ages 16-17 can work at most 28 hours in a school week and 8 hours on a school day.

min_wage.notes: No higher state rate; same as federal.

dmv.name: Rhode Island Division of Motor Vehicles (DMV)

license.full_age: 18, or earlier after 12 months on provisional with no recent tickets
license.notes: Must hold permit 6 months and pass a 33-hour driver ed course (no online courses).

work_permit.required: yes (limited permit for younger teens, starting at 14)
work_permit.issuer: Your city or town school committee
work_permit.notes: Your employer keeps the permit on file at work.

youth_labor.notes: Ages 16-17 in school cannot work after 11:30 p.m. before a school day and are capped at 9 hours a day and 48 a week.

min_wage.notes: Set by law to rise to $17.00 on Jan 1, 2027.

dmv.name: South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV)

license.provisional_min_age: 15 and a half (Conditional license); 16 to under 17 gets a Special Restricted license
license.full_age: 17, or after 1 year on a Conditional or Special Restricted license with no tickets or at-fault crashes
license.notes: Must hold the permit at least 180 days and finish driver's ed (8 classroom hours, 6 driving hours).

state_id.issuer: South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV)

work_permit.notes: SC does not require a work permit. An employer may ask for an age certificate from the state labor department.

youth_labor.notes: SC rules match federal rules. Ages 14-15 have hour limits; 16 and up have no hour limits.

min_wage.notes: No state minimum wage law; the federal $7.25 applies.

voting.preregister_age: 17 if 18 by the next general election

dmv.name: South Dakota Department of Public Safety, Driver Licensing Program

license.provisional_min_age: About 14 and a half or older (Restricted Minor's Permit after holding the instruction permit 275 days, or 180 days with driver's ed)
license.full_age: 16, after 6 months on the Restricted Minor's Permit with no tickets in the last 6 months
license.supervised_hours: 50 hours, 10 at night and 10 in bad weather
license.notes: Restricted permit holders may drive alone 6 a.m. to 10 p.m.

state_id.issuer: South Dakota Department of Public Safety, Driver Licensing Program

work_permit.notes: SD does not issue work permits for minors.

youth_labor.notes: Under 16 cannot work after 10 p.m. on a school night; the stricter of state or federal rules applies.

min_wage.notes: Adjusted every year. Employers may pay new workers under 20 a $4.25 opportunity wage for the first 90 days.

dmv.name: Tennessee Department of Safety and Homeland Security, Driver Services

license.full_age: 17 for Intermediate Unrestricted; full license at 18, or sooner if you graduate high school or get a GED
license.notes: Must hold the learner permit at least 180 days.

state_id.issuer: Tennessee Department of Safety and Homeland Security, Driver Services
state_id.min_age: None stated; children and even infants can get one

work_permit.notes: No work permit, but 16-17 year olds need a signed parent consent form to work until midnight on school nights.

youth_labor.notes: Ages 16-17 cannot work 10 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday to Thursday before a school day without parent consent; minors get a 30-minute break after 6 hours.

min_wage.notes: No state minimum wage law; the federal $7.25 applies.

dmv.name: Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS), Driver License Division

license.full_age: 18 (provisional rules apply to drivers under 18)
license.supervised_hours: 30 hours, 10 at night (part of teen driver's ed)
license.notes: Must hold the learner license at least 6 months.

work_permit.notes: No work permit. A Certificate of Age exists but is not required to start work.

youth_labor.notes: Texas rules for 14-15 year olds are looser than federal; most employers must follow the stricter federal limits.

min_wage.notes: Texas uses the federal minimum wage.

dmv.name: Utah Driver License Division (Department of Public Safety)

license.full_age: 18; the no-friends passenger rule ends after 6 months or at 18
license.notes: A 15-year-old must hold the permit 6 months and until age 16.

state_id.min_age: None stated; under 16 needs a parent or guardian to sign

work_permit.notes: No work permit. Schools help with age certificates if an employer asks.

youth_labor.notes: Minors get a 30-minute meal break within the first 5 hours; federal rules apply where stricter.

min_wage.notes: Same as federal. A $4.25 training wage is allowed for minors for the first 90 days.

dmv.name: Vermont Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV)

license.full_age: 18 (Junior license is for ages 16 and 17); passenger limits end after 6 months
license.notes: Must hold the learner's permit at least 1 year.

state_id.min_age: None; any age (under 18 needs a parent or guardian signature)

work_permit.issuer: Vermont Department of Labor
work_permit.notes: The Vermont labor page links a Child Labor Certificate form.

min_wage.notes: Applies to employers with 2 or more workers; adjusted every Jan 1.

voting.preregister_age: 17 if 18 by the general election (can vote in that primary)

dmv.name: Virginia Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV)

license.provisional_min_age: 16 and 3 months (earliest, after holding the permit 9 months)
license.full_age: 18 (curfew and passenger rules are for drivers under 18)
license.notes: Must hold the learner's permit at least 9 months and finish driver's ed.

state_id.min_age: None stated; DMV offers both a Child ID Card and an Adult ID Card

work_permit.issuer: Virginia Department of Labor and Industry (DOLI)
work_permit.notes: Youth workers 14-15 must get a certificate before doing any work.

youth_labor.notes: Ages 14-15 need a work certificate before starting any job.

min_wage.notes: Adjusted every year.

dmv.name: Washington State Department of Licensing (DOL)

license.permit_min_age: 15 if enrolled in driver training; 15 and a half otherwise
license.full_age: 18 (night and passenger limits end after 1 year of safe driving; license turns regular at 18)
license.notes: Must hold the learner permit at least 6 months.

state_id.min_age: None

work_permit.issuer: Washington Department of Labor & Industries (employer gets a minor work permit; teen gives a parent/school authorization form)
work_permit.notes: Employers must have a minor work permit to hire anyone under 18.

youth_labor.notes: Stricter than federal for 16-17 year olds: max 4 hours a day and 20 hours a week in school weeks.

min_wage.notes: Ages 14-15 may be paid 85% of the state rate; some cities like Seattle are higher.

dmv.name: West Virginia Division of Motor Vehicles (DMV)

license.full_age: 17 (Level 3), after 1 year on Level 2 with no tickets
license.notes: Must hold the Level 1 permit 6 months with no tickets.

state_id.issuer: West Virginia Division of Motor Vehicles (DMV)
state_id.min_age: 2 (Youth ID card covers ages 2 to 15)

work_permit.issuer: West Virginia Division of Labor (school fills out the attendance part)
work_permit.notes: 14 and 15 year olds need an age certificate before taking any paid job.

youth_labor.notes: Minors under 18 cannot work in a bar or serve or sell alcohol where it is drunk on site.

min_wage.notes: Applies where an employer has 6 or more workers at one location; otherwise the federal $7.25 applies.

voting.preregister_age: 17 if 18 by the next general election (can vote in the primary)

dmv.name: Wisconsin Department of Transportation (WisDOT), Division of Motor Vehicles

license.full_age: Limits lift after 9 months with no violations, or at 18
license.notes: Must hold the instruction permit 6 months with no violations.

state_id.min_age: None

work_permit.issuer: Wisconsin Department of Workforce Development (online, $10 fee the employer pays back)
work_permit.notes: Parents apply online; the teen cannot start until the permit fee is paid.

min_wage.notes: Same as federal. Workers under 20 may get a $5.90 opportunity wage for their first 90 days.

dmv.name: Wyoming Department of Transportation (WYDOT), Driver Services

license.full_age: After 6 months on the intermediate permit plus driver's ed, or at 17 without driver's ed
license.notes: Must hold the learner permit at least 10 days.

state_id.min_age: None; residents of any age

work_permit.notes: No work permit; employers keep proof of age on file.

youth_labor.notes: No state rules stricter than federal were listed.

min_wage.amount: $5.15 state rate; most employers must pay the federal $7.25
min_wage.notes: The federal $7.25 applies to most jobs.
